title: Why your phone battery slowly dies, and what speeds it up
description: Every charge cycle wears a lithium-ion battery a little. Heat and sitting at full charge make it worse.

scenes.say: Your phone battery is wearing out, and it started on your very first charge. Here's what's happening inside.

steps: Charging pushes lithium into the anode
A thin film called SEI forms there
scenes.say: Charging pushes lithium ions into a graphite anode. There, a thin film called the SEI layer forms. It thickens with every cycle, and some lithium gets locked away for good. The result is less capacity and higher internal resistance.
Many phones show a battery health number that tracks this wear. It's usually a percentage of the original capacity.
Heat and full charge are the worst combo. Battery University says a battery stored full at 104 degrees Fahrenheit keeps about 65 percent after a year. Stored at 40 percent charge, it keeps about 85.

Consumer lithium-ion cells are commonly rated for 300 to 500 full cycles. Shallower discharges stretch that a lot. And there's no memory effect, so topping up is fine. Follow for more hardware, explained.
